To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the online mode of professional learning was effective in developing teachers' confidence and competence with the technology and in its use as a component of their pedagogy, but that the approach to professional learning was not personalised or self directed.

The online mode of professional learning was effective in developing teachers' confidence in using ICT and their use of ICT in their pedagogy, however, teachers' interaction with the online environment was limited to accessing content and resources, rather than contributing to a co-created community of knowledge.
teachers operated in a self-directed, independent manner and were not inclined to contribute to the generation of collective knowledge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a conceptual framework for self generating online professional development.

the conceptualisation of self generating online teacher communities and their effectiveness in promoting teacher confidence and competence in the use of information and communications technology as a key component in pedagogy.

the development of a self generating network of teachers, where the focus is not only on the development of the teachers' skills but also on their capacity to develop and maintain a community of practice that is self generating and sustaining.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach was not successful in the context of the project.

a personalised, self generating, online teacher professional development program is a feasible and effective means of supporting teachers in developing their confidence and competence to use ICT in the classroom.
the project was not successful in meeting its objectives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the online mode of professional learning was effective in building teacher capacity, but the network was not self generating.

the online mode of PD was effective in promoting the use of technology in teaching, however it is the quality and quantity of interactions between teachers and with content that is critical to the success of the approach.
teachers are capable of self directed professional development, but the process requires more than a single mentor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the concept of self directed learning is a complex one and needs to be carefully considered in terms of the support structures required for teachers to engage with online professional development.
online professional development can be effective and that teachers will engage with the process if they are provided with the necessary support.
a personalised approach to online professional development is feasible, and can be effective.
